title: Caravaggio and chiaroscuro
subject: art
description: **Michelangelo Merisi**, known as Caravaggio, revolutionized painting with brutal realism and extreme light-shadow contrast: chiaroscuro.

hero.hook: Saints with dirty feet, a spotlight: art will never be the same again.

blocks.text: **Michelangelo Merisi**, known as **Caravaggio** (1571-1610), breaks the codes of ideal beauty inherited from the Renaissance. He confronts the sacred and the everyday: beggars, taverns, tired bodies.

His weapon: radical chiaroscuro. Bodies emerge from the darkness as if under a spotlight. This rupture announces the spirit of [[Baroque in painting]] and transforms the spectator into a witness to a drama.

blocks.caption: Caravaggio, painter of genius and figure of turbulent Roman life.

blocks.text: Born near Milan, Caravaggio arrived in Rome around **1593**. His career changed in **1600** with the paintings of the Contarelli chapel, at the Saint-Louis-des-Français church. *The Vocation of Saint Matthew* amazes Rome: the sacred has the face of the street.
In Malta, he was made a knight of the Order, then thrown in prison for having assaulted a superior. He escapes from a fort deemed impregnable with a hemp rope.

His life is as violent as his paintings. In **1606**, during a brawl, he killed **Ranuccio Tomassoni**. Sentenced to death, he fled to Naples, Malta, then Sicily. Hunted and wounded, he died at **38 years old** in [[Porto Ercole]], a few days before a papal pardon.

Caravaggio invented **tenebrism**, an extreme form of chiaroscuro. No more soft light that caresses the forms: an opaque darkness, and bodies that emerge from it with sculptural force. The light is artificial, like a stage spotlight.

blocks.caption: In tenebrism, black focuses the gaze on the drama.

blocks.text: To obtain this lighting, he worked in a workshop with black walls, pierced by a single small skylight high up.

By removing decorations and landscapes, he forces the gaze towards faces and gestures. This light also serves the [[Counter-Reformation]]: the Catholic Church wants to move the faithful. With him, light becomes the grace that strikes the soul without warning.

sections.title: Saints who look like the street

blocks.text: What scandalizes the most is his refusal to idealize. He chooses his models in the street: workers, beggars, courtesans. The Virgin and the apostles have wrinkles, dirty feet, tired bodies.

blocks.caption: The Pilgrim's Madonna: bare, dirty feet in the foreground.

blocks.text: *The Death of the Virgin* is refused: it is said that he took a drowned woman as a model. *The Madonna of the Pilgrims* shocks with the dirty feet of the kneeling poor. He refuses the artifices of [[Mannerism]], this graceful and distorted style which preceded it. For him, salvation is addressed first to the humble.
His first version of *Saint Matthew and the Angel* showed an evangelist with dirty feet, looking uneducated. The sponsors demanded that he repaint it.

He did not found a school, but his style is spreading: **caravagism**. [[Artemisia Gentileschi]] in Italy, Georges de La Tour in France, Zurbarán in Spain, Rubens in Flanders. Later, **Rembrandt** will inherit his shadow poetry, **Velazquez** his dignity of the people.

events.title: Contarelli Chapel
events.detail: Rome discovers The Vocation of Saint Matthew.

events.title: Murder and exile
events.detail: Caravaggio fled Rome, condemned to death.

events.title: Death in Porto Ercole
events.detail: He died at age 38, just before grace.

blocks.text: Forgotten for two centuries, it was rediscovered in the 20th century. Its tight framing and lighting still influence cinema and photography.
Caravaggio (1571-1610) imposed tenebrism and radical social realism. By painting the sacred with models from the street, he became the spiritual father of baroque painting.
